name: bb-mcp-server

tools.name: bitbucket_operation
tools.description:
Execute a Bitbucket operation.

This unified tool provides access to all Bitbucket functionality through a single
interface. The action parameter determines which operation to perform.

Refer to the server instructions for:
- When to use each action
- Recommended workflows and sequences
- Parameter requirements for each action
- Output formats and pagination

action.description: The Bitbucket operation to perform. See server instructions for guidance on when to use each action and how they relate to each other.

repo.description: Workspace/repository slug in 'workspace/repo' format. Falls back to configured defaults when omitted. Used by: pr_list, pr_overview, pr_review, pr_comment_add, pr_comments_list, pr_tasks_sync, pr_upsert, repo_get.

author.description: Filter by author: 'me', a display name/nickname, or an account id. Unset by default -- lists the repo's PRs from all authors. Resolving 'me' costs an extra API call that only user-context credentials can make, so scoping to the caller is opt-in, not the default; call me_whoami to see whether the active credential can resolve it. When a filter resolves but matches nothing, resolved_actors[*].matched is 0 -- an empty `items` alone does not mean the repo has no PRs. Used by: pr_list.

reviewer.description: Filter PRs by reviewer: 'me', a display name/nickname, or an account id. Used by: pr_list.

involving.description: Filter PRs to where this person is author OR reviewer: 'me', a display name/nickname, or an account id. Combines with `author`/`reviewer` (if also given) using AND, not OR. Used by: pr_list.

state.description: Pull request state filter. Used by: pr_list.

limit.description: Maximum items to return. Used by: pr_list, pr_comments_list, workspace_list. For pipe_branch_heads this is pipeline runs scanned (not failures returned), clamped to 1-100.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor. Used by: pr_list, pr_comments_list, workspace_list.

verbosity.description: Response detail level. Used by: pr_list, pr_overview, workspace_list, repo_get.

goal.description: Review depth: 'quick' reports blockers only, 'thorough' also inspects description, diff size and recent comments. Used by: pr_review.

policy.description: Which finding categories to return. Used by: pr_review.

pr.description: Pull request identifier (e.g. '123' or '#123'). Used by: pr_overview, pr_review, pr_comment_add, pr_comments_list, pr_tasks_sync, pr_upsert (for updates).

file.description: File path for inline anchoring. Used by: pr_comment_add, pr_tasks_sync items.

line.description: Line number for inline anchoring. Used by: pr_comment_add.

mentions.description: People to @mention: display name, nickname, or account id. Unresolved or ambiguous mentions block the whole comment. Used by: pr_comment_add.

task_state.description: Filter tasks by state. Used by: pr_tasks_list.

create.description: Tasks to create; each item may include 'text', 'file', and 'line'. Used by: pr_tasks_sync.

resolve.description: Task IDs to resolve. Used by: pr_tasks_sync.

title.description: Pull request title. Used by: pr_upsert.

source.description: Source branch name. Used by: pr_upsert.

destination.description: Destination branch name. Used by: pr_upsert.

reviewers.description: Explicit reviewer identifiers. Used by: pr_upsert.

auto_reviewers.description: Auto-assign reviewers: 'default' (repo defaults), 'all' (workspace members), 'none'. Defaults to 'default' on create only; an update leaves reviewers alone. Used by: pr_upsert.

close_source.description: Close source branch on merge. Used by: pr_upsert.

draft.description: Create/update as draft PR. Used by: pr_upsert.

kind.description: Item type to list. Used by: workspace_list.

slug.description: Repository slug or 'workspace/repo'. Used by: repo_get.

pipeline.description: Specific pipeline ID/number to analyze. Used by: pipe_fail_summary.

include_logs.description: Include full log excerpts in response. Used by: pipe_fail_summary.

days.description: Activity window in days: a branch's most recent pipeline run is dropped if older than this. Default 30. Used by: pipe_branch_heads.

instructions:
## Bitbucket MCP Server

This server provides programmatic access to Bitbucket API v2.0 through a single unified tool.

### Tool Overview

**bitbucket_operation** - Execute any Bitbucket operation by specifying an action parameter.

Available actions:
- pr_list: List pull requests with filtering
- pr_overview: Get PR digest with blockers, comments, diffstat
- pr_review: Generate structured review summary
- pr_comment_add: Add PR comments (inline or general)
- pr_comments_list: List all PR comments with pagination
- pr_tasks_list: List PR tasks with IDs and details
- pr_tasks_sync: Create/resolve PR tasks in one call
- pr_upsert: Create or update pull requests
- pipe_fail_summary: Analyze failing pipeline steps
- pipe_branch_heads: List branches whose head pipeline run failed
- workspace_list: List repos, members, projects, or reviewers
- repo_get: Get repository basics with PR sample
- me_whoami: Get authenticated user identity

### Recommended Workflows

**Pull Request Review Workflow:**
1. Use pr_overview to get PR summary, blockers, and recent comments
2. Use pr_review for structured review guidance with findings
3. Use pr_comment_add to post review comments (can be inline with file/line)
4. Use pr_tasks_sync to create action items from review findings

**Pull Request Creation Workflow:**
1. Use repo_get to confirm target repository and default branch -- this also
   verifies the credential works, and unlike me_whoami it works under every
   supported credential
2. Use pr_upsert with source/destination branches and auto_reviewers="default"
3. Monitor with pr_overview to track approval progress
4. Use me_whoami only when you need the caller's own identity (for an
   author=me filter, say). It reports identity_available=false under
   repository/workspace access-token auth instead of failing, so it is a
   safe probe -- but it answers "who am I", not "is the server up"

**Pipeline Debugging Workflow:**
1. Use pipe_branch_heads when the question is "which branches are broken?" --
   one call covers the repo, it never double-counts a branch, and it never
   reports one whose head has since gone green
2. Use pipe_fail_summary to get recent failing pipelines with log excerpts
3. Review error_kind and fix_hints in the response
4. Check suspected_commit to identify potentially problematic changes
5. Use pr_comment_add to document findings on related PRs

**Workspace Discovery Workflow:**
1. Use me_whoami to list accessible workspaces (empty under access-token auth,
   which is scoped to one repo or workspace already -- check `unavailable`)
2. Use workspace_list with kind="repos" to discover repositories
3. Use repo_get on specific repositories to see details and recent PRs
4. Use workspace_list with kind="members" or kind="reviewers" for team info

### Action-Specific Guidance

**pr_list:**
- Returns paginated list of PRs with compact metadata: id, title, state,
  approvals, tasks_open, comments, reviewers (uuids), author_uuid, updated, url,
  draft
- author is UNSET by default, which lists the repo's PRs from ALL authors.
  author="me" is opt-in: it costs a GET /user that returns 403 under
  repository/workspace access-token auth
- Also filter by reviewer= or involving= (author OR reviewer). Multiple filters
  combine with AND
- resolved_actors in the response echoes what each "me" resolved to, so you do
  not need a separate call to learn your own uuid
- Use state parameter to filter (OPEN, MERGED, DECLINED, SUPERSEDED, ALL)
- Use verbosity="ids" for just PR numbers, "summary" for metadata, "full" for raw API data
- Use cursor parameter from response.next to paginate through results
- Default limit is 10, max is 50 per page

**pr_overview:**
- Provides comprehensive PR digest in a single call
- Returns: PR metadata, blockers (checks, approvals, tasks, conflicts), diffstat, recent comments
- Use this before pr_review to gather context
- Blockers section tells you exactly what's preventing merge
- diffstat_top shows files with most changes (up to 20)
- comments_recent shows last 5 comments with inline anchors

**pr_review:**
- Generates structured review with severity-categorized findings
- Auto-detects blockers from PR status (failing checks, pending tasks, conflicts)
- Returns summary string and array of findings with severity (high/med/low)
- Use findings to guide pr_tasks_sync or pr_comment_add calls

**pr_comment_add:**
- Posts comments to pull requests
- Omit file/line for general PR comments
- Provide file and optionally line for inline comments anchored to code
- Returns comment ID and URL for verification

**pr_comments_list:**
- Lists all comments on a pull request with pagination
- Returns full comment text (up to 300 chars), author, timestamps, and inline anchors
- Use limit parameter to control page size (default 25, max 50)
- Use cursor from response.next to paginate through large comment threads
- Includes parent_id for threaded replies to identify comment hierarchy
- More comprehensive than pr_overview's comments_recent (which only shows last 5)
- Use when you need to review all PR discussion or find specific comments

**pr_tasks_list:**
- Lists all tasks on a pull request with full details
- Returns task IDs needed for pr_tasks_sync resolve operations
- Supports state filtering: OPEN, RESOLVED, or ALL (default)
- Use task_state parameter to filter by task state
- Supports pagination via cursor parameter (default limit 50, max 100)
- Response includes counts: total (count), open, resolved
- Use before pr_tasks_sync to discover task IDs to resolve
- Each task includes: id, state, text, created/updated timestamps, creator, url
- If task is attached to a comment, includes comment_id and comment_url

**pr_tasks_sync:**
- Batch operation for creating and resolving tasks in one call
- create parameter: array of objects with {text, file?, line?}
- resolve parameter: array of task IDs to mark resolved
- Returns created task IDs, resolved task IDs, and remaining open task count
- More efficient than individual task operations

**pr_upsert:**
- Creates new PR or updates existing one
- For creation: title, source branch required; destination falls back to repo main branch
- For updates: provide pr parameter with PR number; all other fields optional
- Auto-detects existing open PR by source/destination branches if pr not provided
- auto_reviewers parameter: "default" (repo defaults, excluding author), "all" (workspace members, excluding author), "none"
- If neither reviewers nor auto_reviewers specified: "default" mode when CREATING,
  and reviewers are left untouched when UPDATING (no reviewers field is sent, so an
  update never re-adds someone a human removed). Pass auto_reviewers explicitly to
  auto-assign on an update.
- Returns reviewers_added and reviewers_skipped in response when using auto_reviewers
- close_source=True to delete source branch after merge
- draft=True to create/update as draft PR; response echoes draft as stored

**pipe_fail_summary:**
- Analyzes recent failing pipelines to identify root causes
- Without pipeline parameter: fetches most recent failed pipelines (up to limit)
- With pipeline parameter: analyzes specific pipeline by ID or build number
- Returns error_kind classification (timeout, test_failure, lint, error, unknown)
- Includes fix_hints array with actionable suggestions
- top_lines contains relevant log excerpts (up to 20 lines)
- Set include_logs=True to get full log excerpts in step.logs field
- suspected_commit helps identify which commit may have introduced the failure

**pipe_branch_heads:**
- Answers "which branches are currently failing?" in one call; fetches no logs
- Finds the newest run per branch first, THEN keeps only the ones still failing.
  pipe_fail_summary filters to FAILED runs first, so it can report one broken
  branch several times and can never show that a branch has since recovered
- limit is the number of pipeline RUNS scanned (newest first), not failures
  returned; clamped 1-100, default 15
- days is an activity window, default 30: a branch whose most recent run is
  older is dropped even if it failed, since it is not actionable
- heads_partial=true means branches below the scan window could still be active,
  so the list may be incomplete -- raise limit if you need certainty. It is
  distinct from logs_partial/top_lines_truncated, which describe log fetching

**workspace_list:**
- kind="repos": Lists repositories with slug, name, privacy, URL, update time
- kind="members": Lists workspace members with UUID, display name, account ID
- kind="projects": Lists projects with key, name, update time
- kind="reviewers": Lists default reviewers for the configured repository (excludes current user)
- Use verbosity="ids" for just identifiers, "summary" for metadata, "full" for raw data
- Supports pagination via cursor parameter
- Default limit is 20, max is 50 per page

**repo_get:**
- Returns repository basics: slug, default branch, permissions, URL
- Includes recent_prs sample (up to 5 most recent PRs)
- Use verbosity="full" to include raw API response
- Useful for discovering repo structure and activity before PR operations

**me_whoami:**
- Returns authenticated user info: UUID, display name, nickname, account ID
- Lists accessible workspaces (up to 20)
- Reports `auth` (the active credential type) and `identity_available`
- NEVER fails on a 403: under repository/workspace access-token auth both
  user-context endpoints are forbidden, so it returns identity_available=false,
  user=null, and names the forbidden endpoints in `unavailable`. That is a
  healthy server under a scoped credential -- do NOT read it as an outage, and
  do not fall back to curl or a CLI on the strength of it
- `ignored_credentials` names a credential that lost on type precedence; a
  non-empty list here explains an unexpected identity_available=false
- Use it to answer "who am I", not "is the server up" -- repo_get answers that
  under every credential
- No parameters required

### Configuration

**Per-Request Configuration (HTTP Headers):**
- X-BITBUCKET-WORKSPACE or X-WORKSPACE: Override workspace
- X-BITBUCKET-REPO or X-REPO: Override repository
- X-BITBUCKET-USERNAME or X-USERNAME: Override username
- X-BITBUCKET-APP-PASSWORD or X-APP-PASSWORD: Override app password
- X-BITBUCKET-ACCESS-TOKEN or X-ACCESS-TOKEN: Repository/workspace access token (Bearer auth)
- Authorization: Basic <credentials>: NOT used as a Bitbucket credential and
  never forwarded -- it may be a gateway password rather than a Bitbucket one.
  Use X-BITBUCKET-USERNAME + X-BITBUCKET-APP-PASSWORD instead
- Authorization: Bearer <token>: NOT used as a Bitbucket credential. A bearer
  token on this header is ambiguous -- it may be the MCP transport's own token
  (MCP_AUTH_TOKEN) rather than a Bitbucket one, and the server cannot tell them
  apart, so it is never forwarded. Use X-BITBUCKET-ACCESS-TOKEN to supply a
  Bitbucket access token per request.
- Any X-BITBUCKET-* credential above takes precedence over the Authorization header.

**Server Defaults (Environment Variables):**
- BITBUCKET_WORKSPACE: Default workspace slug
- BITBUCKET_REPO: Default repository slug
- BITBUCKET_ACCESS_TOKEN: Repository/workspace access token (Bearer auth); preferred, takes precedence over username/app password
- BITBUCKET_USERNAME: Bitbucket username for basic auth
- BITBUCKET_APP_PASSWORD: Bitbucket app password for basic auth
- REQUIRE_CLIENT_CREDENTIALS=true: Prevents fallback to server credentials for HTTP
  requests. Stdio still uses the server's environment credentials.
- MCP_AUTH_TOKEN: Bearer token protecting the HTTP transport. Enforced on HTTP
  requests only; ignored on stdio, where a client cannot present one.

**Repository Resolution:**
The repo parameter accepts multiple formats:
- "workspace/repo-slug": Full specification
- "repo-slug": Uses configured workspace
- null/omitted: Uses configured workspace and repo defaults

### Rate Limits and Constraints

- Bitbucket API rate limits apply (typically 1000 requests/hour for authenticated users)
- Pagination limits: max 50 items per page for list operations
- Pipeline analysis: limit capped at 3 pipelines max for pipe_fail_summary
- Comment text: minimum 1 character required
- PR title: required for creation, must be non-empty

### Performance Optimization

**Use pr_overview instead of multiple calls:**
- Prefer pr_overview over separate calls for PR details, comments, diffstat, and statuses
- Single request provides comprehensive context

**Batch task operations:**
- Use pr_tasks_sync to create and resolve multiple tasks in one call
- More efficient than individual task API calls

**Leverage auto_reviewers:**
- Use auto_reviewers="default" to automatically assign repo default reviewers
- Saves separate calls to fetch and assign reviewers
- Automatically excludes PR author from reviewer list

**Pagination strategy:**
- Start with appropriate limit for your use case (smaller = faster)
- Use cursor from response.next to fetch additional pages only when needed
- Use verbosity="ids" when you only need identifiers

### Error Handling

Common errors and resolutions:
- "Missing workspace/repo": Provide repo parameter or configure defaults
- "PR not found": Verify PR number and repository
- "Unauthorized": Check credentials in headers or environment
- "Validation failed": Review required parameters for the action
- "Rate limit exceeded": Implement exponential backoff and retry

### Security Notes

- Never commit credentials to version control
- Use the X-BITBUCKET-* headers for per-request credentials in multi-tenant scenarios
- Set REQUIRE_CLIENT_CREDENTIALS=true to enforce client-provided credentials; an
  HTTP request that omits the X-BITBUCKET-* headers is then served no credentials
- Do not send a Bitbucket access token on the Authorization header; a bearer token
  there is never forwarded to Bitbucket. Use X-BITBUCKET-ACCESS-TOKEN instead
- Prefer scoped access tokens (BITBUCKET_ACCESS_TOKEN) over app passwords; app passwords are deprecated by Atlassian
- Credentials should have minimal required scopes (pullrequest:write, repository:read)
